conviction_note: Small positive lean (p_up 55) on an abs move of 7.5 (option event move 6.89, own median 6.76, guidance update promised for this print because Ultra is being rolled in). Evidence: a peer that printed after BAH last spoke (CACI, Oct 21: 2.0x book-to-bill, raised guide), a CR in place through Dec 11 so no shutdown overhang like last October's guide cut, and a promised guide update including a >20%-margin acquisition. Against it: the company already guided Q2 down (civil down double digits sequentially, margin step-down), FY EPS consensus sits at the top of the $6.00-6.35 range, the stock ran +8.8% in five days, and the 25d skew of +7.37 pays for downside. The two measurements roughly agree (impact_sum +1.3, scaled +0.75); the gap is the skew and run-up pulling p_up toward 50.
bar: Q2 FY27 adj EPS ~$1.52 and revenue ~$2.82B (Benzinga consensus as quoted in a search snippet, https://it.benzinga.com/quote/BAH/earnings-forecasts, page 403 to direct fetch); a second snippet gives Q2 revenue ~$2.906B, so the revenue bar is disputed. FY27 company guide: revenue $11.2-11.7B, adj EBITDA $1.24-1.29B (~11% margin), adj EPS $6.00-6.35, FCF $825-925M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit992_final.htm). FY EPS consensus $6.31-6.34 (MarketBeat 2026-10-08, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-booz-allen-hamilton-nyse-bah-stock-jumps-62-should-you-buy-2026-10-08/). Prior-year Q2: $2.89B revenue, $1.49 adj EPS. Because the quarterly bar has one source and the revenue bar is disputed, every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest ~7.3% of float, described as declining (Benzinga sentiment page, around early Sept 2026, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BAH/sentiment, snippet only); FINRA settlement 2026-07-15 9.1M shares, 4.2 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bah/short-interest/, snippet only, page 403). Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25d skew +7.37 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.38 (calls dominate open interest), run-up 5d +8.83% and 20d +3.39%, 23.5% below the 52-week high, 91.8% institutional. Sell-side consensus Hold (4 Buy / 7 Hold / 4 Sell), average target $85.62 vs spot $78.2.

findings.finding: CFO on the Q1 FY27 call (2026-07-24) told the market to expect 'a sequential double-digit decline in Civil revenue next quarter due to some contracts that are ending' and a margin step-down 'particularly in Q2'. Q1 Civil was $772M (-16.4% y/y), so roughly $80M+ less Civil revenue in Q2; the Q2 EPS consensus of ~$1.52 against Q1's $1.81 already reflects the step-down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Civil weakness drove the Q2 FY26 print (2025-10-24, -8.86%, with a guide cut) and the 2025-05-23 print (-16.53%, civil job cuts); since civil was guided down in advance, the last three prints rose (+6.76, +3.05, +10.11).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: it sits inside what the company guided and the consensus step-down from $1.81 to ~$1.52 shows it. It is filed because a civil decline larger than 'double digit' sequentially, or no sign of the H2 easing, would be the miss; the skew paying for downside is consistent with the market holding that risk.
findings.independence: Same document as the hiring finding. Q1 release segment numbers: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit991_final.htm

findings.finding: Ultra I&C Mission Solutions ($720M, EBITDA margin 'well above 20%', 'strong double-digit' growth) closed 2026-08-24, inside Q2, and management said on the Q1 call it would roll Ultra into guidance at this October print ('We will update guidance next quarter'). A revenue and EBITDA guide change is therefore mechanically scheduled for this release; revenue was not disclosed (deal financed by the late-July notes, 424B2 2026-07-28/30).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance direction has set this stock's biggest moves: guide cut 2025-10-24 -8.86%, soft FY26 outlook 2025-05-23 -16.53%; guide held with an EPS beat 2026-07-24 +10.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: The close is public, but no revenue figure was ever given, so nobody can model the size of the roll-in; a headline 'raises FY27 revenue/EBITDA guidance' is mechanically likely and is not in the $6.00-6.35 / $11.2-11.7B range the consensus anchors on. Financing question answered: the debt buys a >20%-margin growing business, so the sign is positive or zero, not distress. Partly priced by the +8.8% five-day run-up.
findings.independence: Commitment to update guidance in October is in the Q1 transcript, https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2932789; deal terms in the 2026-06-22 announcement, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000110465926076094/tm2618424d1_ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: FY27 adjusted EPS consensus is $6.31-6.34 against a company guide of $6.00-6.35, i.e. the street already sits at the top of the range; Q1's $0.32 beat ($1.81 vs $1.49) included a $19M pre-tax unrealized venture gain (~$0.12/share) and a lower tax rate, so a merely reaffirmed EPS range would read as no raise despite the beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-24: EPS beat with guide merely reaffirmed bought +10.11%, so the market tolerated a reaffirmation then; 2025-10-24 guide cut -8.86%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar at the top of the range is visible on every terminal; what is not priced is how much of the Q1 beat was the non-operating venture gain the CFO flagged. If the market had priced a no-raise risk, FY consensus would sit at the guide midpoint (~$6.18), not at $6.31-6.34.
findings.independence: Venture gain and tax rate: https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2932789; guidance range: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit992_final.htm

findings.finding: Peer CACI reported its Sep-quarter (Q1 FY27) on 2026-10-21, after BAH last spoke: revenue +8.2% (2.1% organic), adj EPS $7.66 (+11.8%; Benzinga consensus ~$6.62), EBITDA margin 13.3%, book-to-bill 2.0x on $4.8B awards, funded backlog +14.8%, FY27 guide raised on revenue, net income and EPS; its federal civilian revenue fell 3.7% y/y. Shares were up ~3% pre-market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BAH-specific history on peer read-through; BAH's own prints have moved 3-10% on bookings/guidance tone over the last three quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the read-through landed in the same week BAH ran +8.8% (baseline spot struck 13:09 ET on Oct 22, the day of CACI's reaction). Sell-side BAH Q2 estimates were set before it. A same-quarter (Jul-Sep) national-security award environment strong enough for 2.0x book-to-bill supports BAH's national-security segment (~72% of revenue); CACI is defense/intel-heavy, so it says less about BAH's civil book.

findings.finding: Peer SAIC (2026-08-31, quarter to July 31) grew revenue 6.3% (5.3% organic) and raised FY27 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, margin and EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BAH-specific history on peer read-through.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (seven weeks old); filed because it overlaps BAH's July-September quarter only partly and corroborates a firmer federal services demand environment than the one BAH guided into in May.
findings.independence: Different company and document from the CACI finding: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001571123/000157112326000131/saic08312026ex991earningsr.htm

findings.finding: Congress cleared and the President signed (2026-09-01/02) a FY2027 continuing resolution funding the government to 2026-12-11, so there was no lapse on 1 October 2026; a year ago the 2025-10-01 shutdown was under way when BAH reported Q2 FY26 and it cut FY26 guidance (stock -8.86%). BAH's fiscal Q3 (Oct-Dec) is therefore funded through Dec 11 this year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-24 (Q2 FY26, during the shutdown): guide cut, -8.86%.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro fact, widely known, so mostly priced; what it changes is the probability that management again cuts or hedges guidance for a Q3 funding lapse, which a +7.37 put skew still appears to be paying for. Caveat sized in: the Dec 11 expiry falls inside BAH's Q3 and no full-year bill has passed, so management may still flag caution. Proxy: macro-to-company, not confirmed by BAH.
findings.independence: Law-firm outlook dated 2026-10-13 confirms the CR expires 2026-12-11: https://www.joneswalker.com/en/insights/blogs/perspectives/fy2027-federal-funding-appropriations-outlook.html

findings.finding: Truist upgraded BAH to Buy from Hold (~2026-10-08), target $85 from $70, arguing civil declines are near a bottom, national security is underappreciated, and margins benefit from a shift to fixed-price; stock +5-6% that day. Citi ($82 to $77) and Jefferies ($80 to $75) cut targets in the same period; consensus is Hold.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced (the stock moved on the day). Filed as context: a divided sell side (4 Buy/7 Hold/4 Sell) means a civil-bottom confirmation in the release would move holds, which is the mechanism by which a beat gets paid.
findings.independence: MarketBeat on the same move and the target cuts: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-booz-allen-hamilton-nyse-bah-stock-jumps-62-should-you-buy-2026-10-08/

findings.finding: Into the print the stock ran +8.83% in five sessions (to $78.2, from ~$72) while the 25d skew is +7.37 vol points paying for downside and the event-implied move is 6.89%; the bar for a positive reaction has risen in the last week.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 4 of 7 prints up; median absolute 6.76%; the down moves (-8.86, -16.53) both came with guidance cuts.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself (sealed baseline tape and options); filed so the panel sees that the CACI and Truist read-throughs are partly in the run-up. If the run-up were absent the stock would sit near $72 with the same skew.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline (tape.run_up_5d_pct 8.83, options.skew_25d_vol_points 7.37); the 24/7 article shows BAH -1% on Oct 19, so most of the run-up is Oct 20-22.

findings.finding: CFO said on the Q1 call 'We are beginning to accelerate hiring as funding continues to show signs of improvement' after headcount fell to ~30,900 (from 33,400); BAH is a labour-billed business, so Q2 headcount is the leading indicator for the H2 growth the guide depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-05-23 print (-16.53%) came with a 7% workforce cut announcement; headcount has been a headline line.
findings.why_not_priced: Company-guided, so mostly priced; no independent hiring series reached (careers page not checked). A sequential headcount increase in the release would be the first since the cuts and would corroborate the back-half guide.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the civil finding; headcount figures from the Q1 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001443646/000162828026049494/q1fy2027exhibit991_final.htm

findings.finding: Awards in or around the quarter support bookings: GAO denied Serco's protest of BAH's $749M Army Mission Command Training Program contract (July 2026), and the Navy named BAH one of seven awardees on an $827.9M nine-year IDIQ; Q1 book-to-bill was 1.5x with backlog $39.5B (+3.2%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (1.5x book-to-bill, backlog +3.2%) bought +10.11%; backlog commentary has been cited in every positive reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Individually public; the Navy IDIQ is multi-award ceiling value, so the bookings it creates are uncertain. Small.

baseline_tension: The modest positive lean cuts against a +7.37 put skew and sits on top of a +8.8% five-day run-up, so p_up is held at 55; it agrees with the last three prints (all up) and with CACI's same-quarter print.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar single-sourced, revenue bar disputed): kept every finding capped small; the civil decline lands inside what the company guided, so -0.3 moved to -0.2.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the July notes fund Ultra, a >20%-margin growing business, so the Ultra guidance finding stays positive; trimmed +0.7 to +0.6 for the bar cap.

Rule 7 (sign against a strong skew): +7.37 skew pays downside against a positive lean, so p_up moved 56 to 55; the stated reason the market may be wrong is that last October's guide cut came during a shutdown and this year a CR is in place.
Rule 1 (fact vs reaction): reaction history (last three prints up on beats with guide held) did not argue for shrinking further; impact_sum unchanged at 1.3.
